subject: Northstar: private GPU runbook + egress and throughput alignment
messages:
From: Northstar Ops <ops@northstar.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — throughput targets and egress constraints

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We're pulling the procurement docs together and need one thing to finalize staging: concrete throughput targets and any egress/network constraints you need to support our VPC-onprem deployment.

Short version of our expected profile:
- Peak concurrent requests: 2200 (short bursts up to 5 minutes)
- Sustained QPS target: 650 tokens/sec across the fleet (mixed chat + embeddings)
- Typical request size: 60–300 tokens, 95th percentile 800 tokens
- Prefer minimal cross-AZ egress; we'd like to cap outbound to third-party indexers to <= 120 Mbps

Two asks: can you provide a recommended private GPU pool sizing and a short operational runbook (warmup, cache strategy, burst absorption) we can hand to our infra team? Also call out any NIC/egress recommendations and how Redwood handles graceful degradation when we exceed SLA windows.

If easier, share a short spreadsheet; procurement will review network/egress numbers.

Appreciate it — Jordan (on behalf of Northstar ops)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Northstar Ops <ops@northstar.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — throughput targets and egress constraints

Thanks Jordan — good details. Attaching a quick traffic model and a first-pass runbook draft. High level notes below; full recommendations are in the attachment (northstar-traffic-model.csv, redwood-runbook-draft.md).

Quick sizing readout (ballpark):
- Target steady-state capacity to meet 650 tokens/sec: 6x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs behind our private multiplexer (conservative).
- Peak burst headroom (to absorb 2200 concurrent short requests): add 3 warm-buffer GPUs (hot standby) for ~30% burst capacity; total warm-capacity = 9 GPUs.
- If you prefer cost-oriented packing with quantization (int8), you can reduce to ~5 GPUs steady with slightly higher tail latencies.

Networking and egress guidance:
- Recommend 25 Gbps per host NIC when co-locating 2–3 GPUs per server; oversubscription tolerance depends on request size distribution.
- For your <=120 Mbps external indexer cap: we will queue low-priority outbound traffic and prefer batched uploads. Recommend placing outbound indexers in a dedicated egress NAT with rate limits to prevent cross-AZ amplification.

Operational runbook highlights (from draft):
- Warmup: pre-warm KV caches for top-500 prefixes; prefetch model shards during ramp windows.
- Burst handling: our admission controller will prioritize low-latency routes and route excess requests to a lower-cost model variant (quantized) or queue with client-specified timeout.
- Degradation: automatic soft-fallback to smaller model variants + 5–10% token sampling when starvation detected.

Next: looping in Laura and Jonas to sanity-check the numbers and note any customer constraints we should call out for procurement. We'll iterate the runbook and send a version tailored for their infra team.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Northstar Ops <ops@northstar.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — throughput targets and egress constraints

Thanks for the draft, Soojin — nice callout on NIC sizing. A few notes from the deployment/enterprise side before we finalize for procurement:

- Suggest we tighten the warmup recommendation to a two-step window: 15m rapid pre-warm for top prefixes ahead of expected peaks, then a 2h steady warmup for model shard residency. That reduces cold-start tail events.
- For the egress topology diagram (attached), we should add an optional local aggregator instance to batch embeddings uploads; that reduces sustained egress by ~40% in our tests.
- Add explicit SLAs for fallback modes in the runbook (latency tiers + token-drops) so their SRE can sign off.

I also recommend we call out the operator commands for a manual failover (kubectl-like runbook steps) because many on-prem teams prefer explicit playbooks for emergencies. I'll add a short section and push an updated draft.

—Laura
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Northstar Ops <ops@northstar.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — throughput targets and egress constraints

Quick ops check from my side: the 25 Gbps NIC guidance is solid for 2–3 GPUs per server if you run continuous shards. Two implementation notes:
1) If Northstar wants denser GPU packing (4 GPUs per host), we recommend moving to 100 Gbps crossconnect or splitting egress across redundant NICs to avoid head-of-line blocking.
2) For the warm-buffer pool, we'll tag instances with lower preemption priority (if using spot/offers) and attach health probes that evict from the warm pool first.

I'll prepare the small snippet of kubectl-ish commands Laura requested and include a short checklist for on-call teams.

—Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Northstar Ops <ops@northstar.ai>, procurement@northstar.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — throughput targets and egress constraints

Jordan / Northstar team — attaching the updated runbook and a condensed one-page sizing note for procurement. Highlights:
- Recommended initial commit: 9 GPU-equivalents (6 steady + 3 warm) to meet your stated profile with room for 30% burst.
- Network: baseline 25 Gbps per host; 100 Gbps recommended if you want 4 GPUs/host.
- Egress: implement a local aggregator + egress NAT with rate policing (we've attached a topology diagram).

Attachments in this message: redwood-runbook-draft.md (v2), northstar-traffic-model.csv (v2), egress-topology-diagram.png

Next steps:
1) If procurement is happy with the sizing note, we'll prepare an MSA exhibit with sizing and fallback SLAs.
2) We'll schedule a 30–45 min runbook walk-through with your infra team the week of Apr 8.

Thanks — sending the updated artifacts to the Drive as well: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNSTAR-runbook

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
